name: Hearthstone Firearms Ranch SMG HRS-3 'Cattleman'
description:
The HRS-3 Cattleman is Hearthstone's only automatic weapon — a simple, robust 9mm submachine gun designed for agricultural defense against wildlife threats and livestock predators. The weapon features a semi-auto/three-round burst selector with no full-auto option, keeping the rate of fire controlled for untrained ranch operators. The 20-round magazine provides sufficient capacity for most encounters without the bulk of military magazines.

True to Hearthstone's philosophy, the Cattleman has no electronic components. Iron sights, manual safety, mechanical trigger. The weapon is finished in a corrosion-resistant matte ceramic coating designed for years of outdoor storage in ranch buildings and vehicle gun racks. The action is intentionally over-gassed to cycle reliably with dirty, corroded, or low-quality ammunition — the kind of ammunition available at frontier trading posts.

At Φ500, the Cattleman fills the gap between Hearthstone's semi-auto Hearth Guard and the security-oriented weapons of larger manufacturers. It provides controlled automatic firepower to communities that face threats from modified wildlife, feral synthetics, and the occasional human predator. The burst limiter prevents untrained users from dumping ammunition in panic, imposing discipline that their training does not.
specifications:
caliber: 9mm brass-cased
effective_range: 50m
rate_of_fire: Three-round burst, ~750 rpm burst rate
magazine_capacity: 20 rounds
weight: 2.0 kg
tactical_use: The Cattleman provides controlled firepower for non-military users facing close-range threats. The three-round burst delivers enough rounds to neutralize a threat without the ammunition waste of full-automatic fire. The dirty-ammunition tolerance ensures reliability with frontier-quality supplies, and the ceramic coating survives storage conditions that would corrode conventional finishes. Against human threats, the Cattleman's burst fire provides a meaningful improvement over semi-automatic weapons for untrained shooters.
cultural_context: The Cattleman is the ranch weapon — the gun that lives in a truck cab or hangs by the barn door. It is as much a part of frontier agricultural life as fencing tools and water purifiers. Hearthstone designed it for people who think of weapons as tools rather than identities, and the Cattleman's utilitarian no-nonsense design reflects that philosophy. No one boasts about carrying a Cattleman. Everyone is glad to have one when they need it.
story_hooks: Modified predatory wildlife has been attacking frontier ranches with increasing coordination. The standard Cattleman load is no longer sufficient — the ranchers need heavier weapons, but they can't afford them.
Hearthstone received a bulk order for 2,000 Cattlemen from a 'farming cooperative' that doesn't appear to exist. The shipping address is in a Tier 3 urban zone with no agricultural operations.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, utilitarian submachine gun with clean lines and agricultural practicality. The silhouette is blocky and honest—no tactical frills, no chrome aggression. It reads as a tool first, a weapon second. The receiver is noticeably thick-walled, suggesting robust engineering over aesthetics.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length: 38 cm (stock collapsed), 45 cm (stock extended). Barrel length: 12.7 cm. Width at ejection port: 4.2 cm. Height with sights: 11 cm.
physical_description.weight_description: Substantial and balanced—2.0 kg sits comfortably in the hands without tiring. The weight is distributed forward, settling naturally in the palm. Feels like a working gun, not a toy.
physical_description.primary_material: Steel receiver and barrel, polymer handguard and furniture, aluminum fire control group housing
physical_description.finish: Matte ceramic coating in weathered tan-gray, with deliberate micro-texturing to prevent glare. The finish shows practical scratches and handling marks even when new—intentional distressing that suggests the weapon is meant for actual work, not display.
physical_description.color_scheme: Weathered tan-gray ceramic body with flat black polymer grips and handguard. Small brushed aluminum accents around the fire control group. No paint, no logos—purely functional.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer grip with shallow horizontal ribs for positive control in gloved or sweaty hands. Not aggressive, but deliberately non-slip. The texture suggests ranch work: dust-resistant, sweat-resistant.
distinctive_features: Oversized mechanical safety lever—manual and positive, no electronic fail-safes
Ghost-ring iron sights (rear) and hooded front post, both fully mechanical
Three-position selector lever (Safe/Burst/Semi) with crisp detents and tactile feedback
Prominent over-gas adjustment screw on the side of the receiver—designed for field tuning with dirty ammunition
20-round single-stack magazine with witness holes and a heavy steel baseplate
Ventilation slots along the handguard to manage heat during burst fire
Charging handle mounted on the side (ambidextrous), oversized for gloved operation
Integral picatinny rail on top for aftermarket optics (optional—not standard)
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Small Hearthstone Firearms logo (stylized hearth flame) stamped cleanly on the left side of the receiver, just above the magazine well. Serial number engraved (not stamped) on the right side of the receiver. Model designation 'HRS-3' stamped in small letters above the selector. All markings are matte, non-reflective.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained but working-worn. The ceramic finish shows dust residue from storage in gun racks and vehicle mounts. Handling marks on the grip. The interior is clean and lubricated. This is a weapon that spends more time in a ranch armory than in active combat, but is always ready.
